how.eq: Forecast = non-usage charges booked this month + (usage cost month to date ÷ days elapsed) × days in month
how.d: Fixed charges (subscriptions, commitments, support) are counted once; usage is projected at its average daily rate so far. Closed months use actual cost. Computed per cost center, then added up.
Command Center: over budget above 0%, at risk within 3% of budget. Budgets & Forecasts: warning above +2%, critical above +5%.
A straight-line view of the current month, not a seasonal model. Board Pack program run-rates use spend to date ÷ days in the data window × 365.

how.eq: Confidence = mean(share of month elapsed, share of spend from live adapters, allocation coverage, share of closed invoice lines that tie out)
how.d: Rises as the month progresses and as more spend comes from live feeds that reconcile to invoices. Each input is shown next to the score.

how.eq: Forecast year = review-period actuals, annualized, + renewal escalators landing in the forecast year
how.d: Built by vendor for the filing's entity and jurisdiction (PH-05). Renewals and escalators come from the vendor register (PH-06). An invoice exception is flagged because it weakens the support.

There is no machine-learning model and no language model in any figure. Every projection is a fixed formula over billed data, so the same data always gives the same answer, and each figure shows its formula.

how.eq:
Sub-account spike: daily cost > 3 × its average over the prior 14 days, and > $500
API key spike: daily cost > 3σ above its trailing 14-day mean, and > $25
Copilot Studio surge: daily credits ≥ 3 × trailing 7-day average
how.d: Rules run over every day in the data. The excess above the baseline is reported as already spent.

how.eq:
Commitment-eligible spend × 28% (assumed Savings Plan discount)
Standard-tier AI cost × 50% (batch discount)
Idle seats = seat price of seats with no activity in 28 days
how.d: Estimates are opportunities, not savings. They stay labelled as estimates until verified.

how.eq: Verified = 30-day run-rate before the change − run-rate after (14+ days of data)
how.d: Measured on the scope that changed. With less than 14 days of data the estimate is shown as provisional.

how.eq:
Review-period spend failing the reconciliation, approved-policy, GL-account or benefit tests
+ unused share of seat purchases
+ share of a line equal to a savings estimate left unactioned for 60+ days
how.d: Evidence score = cost-weighted share of evidence present. Decision support for the tax team, not a prediction of any tax authority's ruling.

how.eq: Credit = annualized review-period recurring cloud and SaaS fees × the jurisdiction's credit rate
how.d: Claimed where the group already claims these fees; unlock where they qualify but are not yet claimed.

The CostIQ Summary page, and the agent's briefing, are written from the figures on the pages your role can open. CostIQ ranks what matters (forecast against budget, deduction at risk, unclaimed R&D credit, open savings, GxP findings, alerts and invoice exceptions) and writes one sentence per point. Every figure links to the panel or row it comes from, and the numbered chips list the source pages. Saved wording is used while the figures behind it are unchanged; every figure in it is still read live from the linked page.

Your question is matched to one of the tested use cases by keyword ranking (BM25), parameters such as periods and providers are read from the text, and the use case runs in your scope. Nothing is generated; if nothing matches, CostIQ says so.

terms: The FinOps Foundation's open billing standard. Every provider's bill is loaded into the same FOCUS columns, so AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Snowflake and AI vendors compare line for line.
What the invoice charges for a line.
Cost after discounts and with commitment purchases spread over the usage they cover. Most CostIQ figures use it.
Price at public rates / at your negotiated rates. List − contracted = negotiated discount.
Savings Plan, reservation, committed-use discount or provisioned AI throughput (PTU) paid for in advance. Unused commitment is cost with no usage behind it.
Spend projected to a year from a recent period.
Where cost is reported, from tags, approved allocation rules or split-cost data. Each person sees only their own.
An approved, effective-dated rule that splits shared cost (for example by enrolled patients or trial sites). One person submits, another approves.
The company in the group that bears a cost, and the tax jurisdiction it is reported in.
Technology cost charged from the shared-services entity to the operating entities, on a documented key.
opex, capital, or qre (qualifying research expenditure for R&D credits).
The actual period a tax filing rests on, and the year it projects to.
A tax authority's information request. CostIQ drafts the answer from a tested use case; someone else approves it.
A ZIP of the filing's evidence. Its SHA-256 fingerprint is sealed in the decision ledger, so anyone can check it later.
Money already spent on waste or error (spikes, idle capacity, invoice mismatches).
A saving that has not happened yet. Never added to verified savings.
Spend on a workload that fails a compliance check. Reported separately; never summed with savings.
Identified → approved → implemented → verified, with a different person signing each step.
Good practice rules (clinical, laboratory, manufacturing) for systems that affect product quality or patient safety.
US and EU rules for electronic records and signatures in regulated systems.
The documented check that a GxP system, or AI used in GxP work, does what it should. Systems are re-reviewed on a schedule.
Encryption keys the company controls, so the provider cannot read patient data.
The contract terms a GxP vendor must sign: quality, audit rights, change notification, data integrity.
Technology operating cost ÷ patients enrolled in trials, annualized.
Whoever submits a finding, policy, optimization or examiner response cannot approve or verify it.
A hash-chained log of every approval. Changing an old entry breaks the chain, which the Governance page checks.
A tested, named analysis with its SQL and formula. CostIQ runs 145 of them.
In CostIQ: computed from data CostIQ holds. Partial: part of the section needs a feed or an approval. Needs data: the missing input is named; nothing is estimated in its place.
